name: Durable Approval Boundary
summary: Bind human authorization to an immutable action request and enforce external idempotency independently from framework resume.
context: A tool or Workflow node can create an irreversible, regulated or financially consequential effect.
Approval can expire, be replayed or arrive from the wrong principal.
forces: A scoped approval envelope and ledger cost more than a confirmation boolean.
Durable storage and partial-commit recovery become production dependencies.
Exact request binding can require reapproval after a material edit.
decision: Treat ADK confirmation or RequestInput as interrupt transport, not authorization.
Validate approver, action scope, request digest, policy version, decision and expiry before execution.
Enforce one external effect per action ID in the side-effect service.
implementation: Construct and hash the immutable action request before interrupting.
Authenticate the approval channel outside the model.
Persist decision and effect evidence separately.
Test fresh-object resume, rejection, expiry, tampering and later-run replay.

observable_contract.statement: Approval binds authenticated approver, action ID/type, full request digest, policy version and expiry.
Rejected or invalid approval cannot call the side-effect service.
A valid response resumes with fresh runtime objects and executes exactly one approved action.
Later-run confirmation replay can re-enter the tool but one action ID produces at most one external effect.

failure_modes.statement: Natural-language instructions ask the model to wait but do not prevent the tool call.
An after-tool filter hides output but cannot undo the external effect.
confirmed=true carries no approver identity, request integrity, policy version or expiry.
Session history or consumed confirmation state is mistaken for side-effect idempotency.

counterexamples.context: A reversible low-risk read has a deterministic authorization policy.
counterexamples.preferred: Apply the authorization rule directly without human approval.

counterexamples.context: The tool is over-privileged or accepts unsafe arguments.
counterexamples.preferred: Reduce privilege and validate arguments; approval is not a substitute.

adk_versions.notes: FunctionTool ToolConfirmation and Workflow RequestInput pause/resume were exercised at the pinned commit.
The authorization envelope and idempotency contract are portable; interrupt and replay transport need adapter tests.

source_evidence.claim: ToolConfirmation carries confirmed, hint and payload but no approver identity, request digest or expiry.
Before-tool replacement can prevent execution while after-tool replacement occurs after the tool effect.
Confirmation resume validates original call identity and arguments before re-executing the tool.
Workflow HITL transports RequestInput interrupts and resume responses at node scope.

lab_evidence.claim: Rejected, expired, unauthorized and tampered approvals produce zero side effects.
Fresh Agent and Runner objects resume one valid approved payment.
Later-run replay re-enters the tool while the external ledger retains one effect.
Prompt-only and after-tool variants demonstrate enforcement that occurs too late or not at all.

rejected_decisions.decision: Treat ToolConfirmation confirmed=true as a complete business authorization.
rejected_decisions.reason: The transport does not authenticate the approver, bind policy scope or guarantee external idempotency.
rejected_decisions.replacement: Validate a scoped application approval envelope and execute through an action-ID idempotent service.
